package_info.package_versions: 1.2.1 and all other published versions (20+ updates since Dec 11, 2022)
package_info.why_malicious: The package masquerades as a legitimate SentinelOne SDK client but contains trojanized code that steals sensitive developer data and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled IP address. It targets developer environments to harvest secrets, SSH keys, and cloud credentials.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when api.py is imported or used by the SDK client)
execution_context.file_location: management/mgmtsdk_v2_1/services/api.py (and similar paths in the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Harvests sensitive files (shell histories, SSH keys, git configs, AWS/Kube configs) from all user home directories and uploads them to a remote server controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code systematically collects sensitive files unrelated to the SDK's legitimate purpose and exfiltrates them to an external IP address.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate SDK client should not access or transmit user shell histories, SSH keys, or cloud configuration files. It should only interact with the SentinelOne API as documented.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or migration tools may access similar files, but only with explicit user consent and never transmit them to unknown servers.
key_indicators: Access to multiple sensitive files across all home directories
Use of hardcoded external IP address for data exfiltration
No user notification or consent for data collection

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious SentinelOne package, triggering execution of api.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs in the context of the developer's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in api.py collects sensitive files from all user home directories.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is aggregated for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is exfiltrated to the attacker's server at 54.254.189.27.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to developer secrets, credentials, and configuration files.

behavioral_signatures: Python packages accessing multiple sensitive files in user home directories
Unexpected network requests to hardcoded external IP addresses during import or runtime
Exfiltration of data to non-canonical endpoints
file_indicators: api.py files in management/mgmtsdk_v2_1/services/ or similar paths within a SentinelOne-named package
Presence of code that enumerates /home directories and accesses .ssh, .aws, .kube, .gitconfig, shell history files
network_indicators: Connections to /api/v1/file/upload endpoints not associated with SentinelOne
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages (especially those named similarly to trusted vendors) that access sensitive files in user home directories and make outbound network requests to unknown or hardcoded IP addresses. Flag any package that attempts to exfiltrate data to endpoints not associated with the legitimate vendor. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized access to SSH keys, cloud configs, and shell histories by non-privileged processes.
